query: Research on refractory multicomponent alloys has emphasized exceptional strength at room and elevated temperatures, while mechanical assessment has relied mainly on compression and has included relatively few tensile studies. WFeNiMo fragments released more chemical energy than tungsten-alloy fragments in thin-steel-target penetration tests, and HfZrTiTa0.53 was reported at 786 MPa yield strength, 1314 MPa compressive strength, and 13.5% terminal strain. This evidence establishes strength and energetic promise but leaves limited tensile ductility, load-bearing reliability, and processability unresolved. Subject to preserving strength and impact-triggered energy release, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention for HfZrTiTa0.53 that could improve tensile ductility and uniform elongation? Include the intervention, causal mechanism, directional or quantitative outcomes relative to the reported baseline, the applicable temperature, loading mode, and strain-rate limits, prior evidence from the cited studies, and matched compression, tension, and impact tests with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Thermomechanical grain refinement via four passes of equal‐channel angular pressing (ECAP) at 600 °C will reduce the average grain size of HfZrTiTa0.53 to below 1 µm, increase room‐temperature uniform tensile elongation to >5% while preserving yield strength within 10% of the 786 MPa baseline, and maintain impact energy release in thin‐steel‐target tests within 10% of the as‐cast alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐cast HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory alloy; average grain size ∼10 µm; compressive yield strength 786 MPa; compressive fracture strain 13.5%; no published tensile elongation data.
generation.conditions: Room temperature; quasi‐static loading for tension and compression (strain rate ∼10⁻³ s⁻¹); impact tests at ∼600 m/s projectile velocity
generation.structural_mediator: Reduction of average grain size to <1 µm
generation.mechanism: Increased grain‐boundary area promotes dislocation storage and uniform slip activity, delaying localization and enhancing uniform elongation without significant loss of strength
generation.predicted_outcome: Uniform tensile elongation >5% (versus assumed <2% baseline); tensile and compressive yield strengths within ±10% of 786 MPa; fragment energy release in steel‐target penetration within ±10% of as‐cast alloy
generation.baseline: As‐cast: compressive yield strength 786 MPa; compressive fracture strain 13.5%; assumed tensile uniform elongation <2%
generation.boundary: Applies to room‐temperature tests at strain rates 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹ and impact velocities ~600 m/s; not validated at elevated temperature or extreme high strain rates (>10³ s⁻¹).
generation.uncertainty: Medium; grain‐refinement effects on compressive ductility are established in similar refractory alloys but direct tensile data on HfZrTiTa0.53 are lacking.

falsification_experiment.design: Process HfZrTiTa0.53 by four‐pass ECAP at 600 °C; characterize grain size; perform matched quasi‐static compression and tensile tests at room temperature (10⁻³ s⁻¹) and impact penetration tests at 600 m/s.
measurements: Fragment energy release in steel‐target tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if uniform tensile elongation remains <3%, or if yield strength in tension or compression drops >20% below baseline, or if impact energy release decreases >10%.
